q: The convoy ______ the checkpoint when the ambush started.
e: An action in progress that is interrupted takes the past progressive.

q: By the time the reinforcements arrived, the enemy ______.
e: An earlier action in the past takes the past perfect.

q: Our unit ______ joint exercises with NATO since 2019.
e: since + an action that is still going on: present perfect progressive.

q: Water ______ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
e: A general truth takes the present simple.

q: I ______ my report before the briefing starts tomorrow.
e: Completed before a future moment, so future perfect.

q: The ship ______ port at 0600 tomorrow, according to the schedule.
e: An official timetable takes the present simple, even for the future.

q: He ______ in the operations centre for three years before he was transferred.
e: A duration leading up to a past event.

q: This time next week we ______ across the Mediterranean.
e: An action in progress at a future moment.

q: She ______ the radio when the alarm sounded.
e: A past setting interrupted by another action.

q: I ______ him since the last staff meeting.
e: since -> present perfect.

q: The colonel ______ just ______ the operations order.
e: just -> present perfect.

q: When I got to the pier, the ship ______ already ______.
e: already marks an earlier past action.

q: We usually ______ our equipment on Fridays.
e: usually marks a habit.

q: He ______ to Washington three times this year.
e: This year is not finished yet: present perfect.

q: Before the war ______, the country had been prosperous.
e: Narration in the past.

q: By 2030 the fleet ______ its modernisation programme.
e: By + date future -> future perfect.

q: I ______ my keys. I can't open the door.
e: The present result of a past action.

q: My car ______ down twice this month.
e: This month is not finished yet: present perfect.

q: The sun ______ in the east.
e: A law of nature takes the present simple.

q: I ______ that film. Let's watch something else.
e: already -> present perfect.

q: When I ______ home tonight, I will call you.
e: After when with future meaning, use the present simple.

q: The squadron ______ for Tunis as soon as the weather improves.
e: The main clause is in the future.

q: She ______ in this office since she graduated.
e: since -> present perfect.

q: At 8 o'clock yesterday evening we ______ the frigate.
e: A precise past time with an action in progress.

q: He ______ smoking two years ago.
e: ago -> simple past.

q: Don't call at 7 - I ______ the evening brief then.
e: An action in progress at a future moment.

q: I ______ him for twenty years and I still trust him.
e: know is a state verb, so duration takes the present perfect.

q: We ______ our new radios by the end of last year.
e: by the end of last year -> past perfect.

q: The delegation ______ tomorrow morning at 0900.
e: A fixed schedule takes the present simple, even for the future.

q: While the officers ______, the crew prepared the launch.
e: Two past actions happening at the same time: past progressive (while they were talking).

q: He hasn't answered my email ______.
e: Negative + present perfect takes yet.

q: Once the order ______, we will execute it immediately.
e: Once + present carries a future meaning.

q: She ______ the door when she heard the explosion.
e: A long action that is interrupted.

q: They ______ each other since the academy.
e: since -> present perfect.

q: The patrol ______ back before dark yesterday.
e: yesterday -> simple past.

q: I ______ my uniform when the phone rang.
e: A past setting interrupted by another action.

q: We ______ this system for six months now.
e: for + now -> present perfect progressive.

q: Next June he ______ in the Navy for twenty years.
e: A duration completed by a future moment.

q: The instructor ______ us how to plot a bearing yesterday.
e: yesterday -> simple past.

q: Do you know where he ______ his career?
e: A past fact tied to a specific date.

q: I'm exhausted. I ______ since 5 a.m.
e: The cause of the present result.

q: He ______ his medal in a ceremony last spring.
e: last spring -> simple past.

q: You ______ salute a senior officer; it is a regulation.
e: An absolute obligation, such as a regulation: must.

q: Visitors ______ not enter the restricted area.
e: A formal written prohibition: may not.

q: She ______ speak three languages fluently.
e: Ability: can.

q: He ______ have missed the bus; he is never late.
e: Deduction negative -> can't have.

q: You ______ have told me earlier - I would have helped.
e: Reproach about the past -> should have.

q: We ______ to report at 0700 sharp.
e: ought to + infinitive.

q: You ______ worry; the situation is under control.
e: No necessity: needn't.

q: He ______ be at the office; his car is outside.
e: A logical conclusion that something is true: must.

q: ______ we begin the briefing now?
e: A suggestion with we takes Shall.

q: Recruits ______ to have a haircut when they arrive.
e: What other people expect you to do: be supposed to.

q: I ______ get up at five when I was at the academy.
e: A past obligation: had to.

q: She ______ have taken the earlier flight, but she chose not to.
e: A past possibility that did not happen: could have.

q: Passengers ______ fasten their seat belts during take-off.
e: A compulsory instruction.

q: He ______ not have signed the document; it was invalid anyway.
e: An unnecessary action that was done takes needn't have.

q: We ______ eat out tonight if you like.
e: Suggestion -> could.

q: He ______ pass the ECL; he has studied very hard.
e: Probability: ought to.

q: You ______ better check the coordinates twice.
e: had better + the simple form of the verb (had better check).

q: He was finally ______ to board the aircraft.
e: Permission given on one occasion in the past: was allowed to.

q: They ______ have been friends; they had never met.
e: A negative conclusion about the past: couldn't have.

q: The plants ______ watering twice a week.
e: need + V-ing carries a passive meaning.

q: Is he ______ to understand the technical manual?
e: Asking about probability: be likely to.

q: You ______ walk on the grass in the parade ground.
e: A prohibition: mustn't.

q: She ______ at least have warned us about the delay.
e: Criticism of the past -> could have.

q: We ______ to reply to the invitation today.
e: ought to.

q: He ______ have won the tender; the results are not out yet.
e: A possibility about the past: may have.

q: The report ______ by the chief of staff yesterday.
e: Past passive.

q: Two suspects ______ questioned at the moment.
e: Present progressive passive.

q: This bridge ______ in 1952.
e: A date in the past: past passive, was built.

q: The keys ______ behind, apparently.
e: Perfect modal passive.

q: Skis ______ here since 1964.
e: since -> present perfect passive.

q: Acupuncture ______ by the Chinese thousands of years ago.
e: Past passive.

q: Neil ______ class representative last week.
e: Verb + object turned into the passive.

q: Barrow ______ to have left Wales last week.
e: Passive + perfect infinitive.

q: Your hair ______ cutting.
e: need + V-ing carries a passive meaning.

q: He was hit on the head ______ a hammer.
e: Instrument -> with.

q: My purse was found ______ one of the cleaners.
e: Agent -> by.

q: All the preparations ______ by the time the guests arrived.
e: Past perfect passive.

q: Petrol prices ______ to rise tomorrow.
e: Present perfect passive.

q: Nobody can beat him. -> He ______ be beaten.
e: Modal passive: can't be beaten.

q: The tree ______ during the storm.
e: Fall is intransitive, so it has no passive.

q: If you heat ice, it ______.
e: Zero conditional: general truth.

q: If we leave now, we ______ the ferry.
e: First conditional: a likely result.

q: If I were the commanding officer, I ______ the schedule.
e: Type 2 conditional: unreal present.

q: If they had left earlier, they ______ the attack.
e: Type 3 conditional: unreal past.

q: If he has time, he ______ help you.
e: First conditional with a modal.

q: If that thief hadn't tricked me, I ______ in prison now.
e: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

q: If I had learnt to sail, I ______ in the regatta now.
e: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

q: Unless the weather ______, the exercise will be cancelled.
e: Unless + present simple.

q: I would call him if I ______ his number.
e: Second conditional: if + past simple.

q: ______ you had told me, I could have helped.
e: Third conditional introduced by if: if + past perfect, could have + past participle.

q: We will postpone the sortie ______ the fog lifts.
e: unless = if ... not (we will postpone it if the fog does not lift).

q: If you had left the party early, we ______ never ______.
e: Third conditional with might.

q: Take a spare battery ______ the radio fails.
e: Precaution -> in case.

q: Had I known the truth, I ______ differently.
e: Inversion (Had I known) = third conditional.

q: If you ______ me, the mission would have failed.
e: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

q: I wish I ______ more time to prepare.
e: wish + past simple expresses a present regret.

q: If only I ______ listened to your advice!
e: If only + past perfect expresses regret about the past.

q: Should you need assistance, ______ the duty officer.
e: Formal inversion of the first conditional (Should you need = If you need) followed by an imperative.

q: "I will call you," she said. -> She said she ______ call me.
e: will -> would.

q: "We have finished," they said. -> They said they ______ finished.
e: Present perfect -> past perfect.

q: "Do you like tea?" -> He asked her ______ she liked tea.
e: A yes/no question is reported with if or whether.

q: "I'm sorry I was rude," he said. -> He apologised ______ rude.
e: apologise for + V-ing.

q: "You stole my bag!" -> She accused me ______ her bag.
e: accuse sb of + V-ing.

q: "I didn't break it," he said. -> He denied ______ it.
e: deny + V-ing.

q: "I'll be there early," he said. -> He promised ______ there early.
e: promise + to-infinitive.

q: "Shall I carry your bags?" -> He ______ to carry my bags.
e: Reporting an offer (Shall I ...?): offer to do something.

q: "You should see a doctor." -> He ______ me to see a doctor.
e: advise sb to.

q: "Water boils at 100 C," he said. -> He said water ______ at 100 C.
e: A general truth does not change tense in reported speech.

q: "I saw him yesterday." -> She said she had seen him ______.
e: yesterday -> the day before.

q: "I'm leaving tomorrow." -> He said he was leaving ______.
e: tomorrow -> the following day.

q: "Come here," she said. -> She told me to ______ there.
e: come becomes go in reported speech.

q: "I can swim," he said. -> He said he ______ swim.
e: can -> could.

q: "You needn't come." -> He said I ______ come.
e: needn't -> didn't need to.

q: I wonder ______ he will accept the offer.
e: wonder + whether / if.

q: "It's a brilliant idea!" she said. -> She ______ that it was a brilliant idea.
e: Exclamation -> exclaim.

q: "Don't go near the cliff." -> He ______ me not to go near the cliff.
e: Reporting a warning (Don't ...): warn someone not to do something.

q: He insisted ______ paying for the meal.
e: insist on + V-ing.

q: He has been in the Navy ______ 2008.
e: since + a starting point in time (since 2008); for + a length of time (for six years).

q: We waited ______ two hours.
e: for + a duration.

q: The briefing starts ______ 0800.
e: at + an exact time (at 0800).

q: The exercise takes place ______ July.
e: in + a month (in July).

q: The ceremony is ______ Monday.
e: on + a day (on Monday).

q: He is responsible ______ logistics.
e: responsible for.

q: He was accused ______ negligence.
e: accuse of.

q: Congratulations ______ your promotion!
e: congratulations on.

q: We arrived ______ the airport at midnight.
e: arrive at + a specific place (at the airport).

q: They arrived ______ Tunisia last week.
e: arrive in + a country or a large city (in Tunisia).

q: This decision is different ______ the previous one.
e: different from.

q: He apologised ______ being late.
e: apologise for.

q: I am not interested ______ that proposal.
e: interested in.

q: The ship is capable ______ sustained operations.
e: capable of.

q: We must comply ______ the rules of engagement.
e: comply with.

q: He succeeded ______ passing the ECL.
e: succeed in + V-ing.

q: The meeting was postponed ______ Friday.
e: postpone until.

q: She insisted ______ seeing the commander.
e: insist on.

q: They are aware ______ the risks.
e: aware of.

q: The base is protected ______ attack.
e: protect from.

q: He was praised ______ his courage.
e: praise sb for.

q: The meeting was ______ off because of the storm.
e: call off = cancel.

q: Please ______ out this form before you leave.
e: fill out / fill in = complete a form.

q: We ran ______ of fuel halfway through the patrol.
e: run out of = have none left.

q: Look ______ the word in the glossary.
e: look up = to search for in a reference work.

q: The commission is looking ______ the incident.
e: look into = investigate.

q: Another company has taken ______ our supplier.
e: take over = buy a company or take control of it.

q: We are dealing ______ your complaint.
e: deal with = handle, take action on.

q: The soldiers were told to carry ______ the mission.
e: carry out = perform (an order, a task).

q: Please ______ up; I can't hear you on this channel.
e: speak up = speak louder.

q: He ______ down the offer of a new posting.
e: turn down = refuse.

q: The generator ______ down during the exercise.
e: break down = stop working (a machine or a vehicle).

q: I can't ______ up with this noise any longer.
e: put up with = supporter.

q: The alarm went ______ at three in the morning.
e: go off = start suddenly (an alarm) or explode (a bomb).

q: Try to ______ down the main points of the brief.
e: take down = to write down.

q: He was ______ up in a traffic jam.
e: be held up = be delayed.

q: There isn't ______ fuel left in the tank.
e: fuel is uncountable, so much.

q: How ______ officers attended the conference?
e: officers is countable, so many.

q: We have ______ time before the briefing.
e: time is uncountable with a negative sense, so little.

q: Only ______ candidates passed the test.
e: candidates is countable, so a few.

q: ______ information you gave me was very useful.
e: Something already known (a definite reference) takes the.

q: He is ______ honest officer.
e: A silent h (honest, hour) takes an.

q: She plays ______ piano very well.
e: Playing a musical instrument takes the (the piano).

q: We travelled to ______ United States last year.
e: A plural country name takes the.

q: ______ of the two proposals is acceptable.
e: Neither means not either of the two.

q: There were ______ people in the hall than expected.
e: people is countable, so fewer.

q: He spent ______ money on equipment.
e: money is uncountable.

q: Each of the candidates ______ a personal file.
e: Each takes a singular verb.

q: ______ the officers were present at the ceremony.
e: All of the takes a plural verb.

q: Is there ______ coffee left?
e: Question -> any.

q: This frigate is ______ than the previous one.
e: Short adjective, so the comparative takes -er.

q: It is the ______ decision he has ever taken.
e: Long adjective, so the most.

q: She is not ______ experienced as her colleague.
e: as ... as.

q: It's high time we ______ the procedure.
e: It's time + past subjunctive.

q: The officer ______ briefed us has just retired.
e: Human subject, so who.

q: The ship ______ hull was damaged returned to port.
e: Possession -> whose.

q: This is the report ______ I mentioned yesterday.
e: A thing, not a person: which or that.

q: Not only ______ he arrive late, he also forgot the file.
e: Inversion after Not only.

q: Never before ______ such a request.
e: Inversion after Never before.

q: Hardly ______ we left when the storm broke.
e: Hardly ... when.

q: The more you practise, ______ you become.
e: Double comparative.

q: He denied ______ the classified file.
e: deny + V-ing.

q: The officer in charge of a ship is the ______.
e: Commanding officer = the officer in command of a ship or a unit.

q: A written order describing a mission is an operations ______.
e: Operations order (*opord*).

q: Soldiers live in ______ on a base.
e: Barracks = the buildings where soldiers live.

q: Anti-submarine warfare is abbreviated ______.
e: ASW = anti-submarine warfare.

q: The person who steers the ship is the ______.
e: Helmsman = the person who steers a ship.

q: A short meeting to give information is a ______.
e: Briefing.

q: To leave a military post without permission is to ______.
e: Desert = leave military service without permission.

q: Equipment and supplies are handled by ______.
e: Logistics.

q: The rules that govern the use of force are the rules of ______.
e: Rules of engagement.

q: A ______ is a group of ships operating together.
e: Task force = a group of ships or units brought together for one mission.

q: Information about the enemy is called ______.
e: Intelligence.

q: To move troops away from a dangerous area is to ______ them.
e: Evacuate.

q: A ______ officer deals with staff duties at headquarters.
e: Staff officer.

q: The chain of ______ defines who reports to whom.
e: Chain of command.

q: An aircraft that has no pilot on board is a ______.
e: Drone / *uav*.

q: A ______ is a formal investigation of an incident.
e: Inquiry.

q: The ship's ______ is the officer second in command.
e: Executive officer.

q: To ______ a ceasefire means to respect it.
e: Observe a ceasefire.

q: Casualties are people who are ______ in an operation.
e: Casualties.

q: A ______ is a temporary stop in fighting.
e: Truce = an agreement to stop fighting for a time.

q: Deborah ______ a car. She goes to work by bus.
e: Negative present with have as a full verb, so doesn't have.

q: That movie ______ very good. The story is boring.
e: The adjective good goes with be in the negative, singular.

q: She ______ her homework quickly!
e: Verb ending in -sh takes *es*.

q: I'm sorry sir; we ______ accept credit cards.
e: Negative of a lexical verb in the present takes don't.

q: Peter and Douglas ______ a minute ago.
e: a minute ago -> simple past irregulier.

q: My sister ______ in Milan for two months last year.
e: last year + a state (be): simple past, was.

q: Deborah ______ to Wales three years ago.
e: three years ago -> simple past.

q: After years as a classroom assistant, Verena finally ______ a teacher.
e: An action completed in the past.

q: Although Rory spent four years studying math, he ______ understand it very well.
e: Past context -> didn't.

q: That movie ______ very good. The story was boring.
e: Singular subject in the past, so wasn't.

q: She ______ her homework quickly yesterday!
e: yesterday: simple past of a regular verb.

q: He ______ to the cinema five times last month.
e: last month -> went.

q: She ______ her decision this morning.
e: The only past-tense verb among the options.

q: Saaid ______ breakfast yesterday morning.
e: Negative of the simple past takes didn't + base form.

q: The instructor ______ how to handle a gun.
e: Narration in the past.

q: When Fiona's fever got very high, she ______.
e: Sequence of tenses with got, so the simple past.

q: The petty officer ______ the seaman sleeping on watch last night.
e: Irregular past of catch -> caught.

q: Don't *stare at* him like that.
e: *Stare* = to look at something or someone for a long period of time

q: The weather was very *mild* throughout our entire vacation.
e: mild = moderate = not extreme = in the middle of a range

q: Which of the following can *hover*?
e: *Hover* = to stay in the air in one stationary place (for a while)

q: We always *store* our sweaters and coats during the summer.
e: *Store* = put away, put in storage, put out-of-sight, maybe in the closet or in a trunk

q: The gym is located *beyond* the post office.
e: *Beyond* = past, on the far side of

q: The score was *tied* at the end of regulation time.
e: *Tied* = to be even, to be the same. The score was *tied* at 2-2. His home run in the eleventh inning finally broke the 3-3 tie.

q: Othello *choked* Desdemona.
e: choke = strangle = stop the passage of air at the throat

q: In our ethics class, we were taught that a good leader should have _____.
e: *Integrity* = honesty = sincerity = inner truth = basic morality

q: It's time to *hoist* the flag.
e: *Hoist* is to raise something up in the air. You *hoist* a flag. A crane can *hoist* cargo.

q: The *knee* is to the *leg* as the _____ is to the *arm*.
e: The knee is the joint in the middle of the leg, just as the *elbow* is the joint in the middle of the arm.

q: My aunt is no spring chicken. She is not _____.
e: *Spring chicken* = young (as young as a chicken born during the most recent spring) Always in the negative.

q: A pecking order is an organization is _____.
e: pecking order = in the barnyard, the bigger powerful birds "peck" on the smaller her place.

q: A major *is lower in rank than* a colonel.
e: *To be under* = to be the subordinate = to be lower = to be underneath in the chain- of-command

q: We _____ to my brother's house tomorrow.
e: The time word "tomorrow" needs *future tense*.

q: We _____ right now.
e: Time words "right now" require *present perfect*. *We are doing* something.

q: We _____ a lot of songs at last night's party.
e: "Last night" requires the *past tense*.

q: My left leg _____.
e: Current state or condition. *Present tense*. Third person singular.

q: Tomorrow, I will _____ home.
e: After a *modal*, you use the *simple form* of the verb. *I will do* something tomorrow.

q: I may _____ to the movie tomorrow.
e: Remember: put the *simple form* of the verb after a modal.

q: Yesterday, I _____ my old friend.
e: Past tense irregular verb *meet met*

q: He _____ a large meal for his entire family yesterday.
e: Regular verb past tense *he cooked*

q: I _____ right now.
e: "Right now" requires *present perfect*. Subject "I" requires AM.

q: My friend _____ tomorrow.
e: We can express the *future tense* with the *present progressive*. Something *is happening* tomorrow.

q: I _____ that movie already.
e: Here, the "already" requires *present perfect*. *I have done* something already.

q: He likes Nevada, _____?
e: Tag question. Affirmative in the main clause requires negative in the tag.

q: If I had a million dollars, I _____ a new car.
e: "*If*" clause. Present unreal. I do not have the money, but *if I had it a* modal like "would" requires *simple form* after it. *I would buy* something.

q: While I was reading the paper, the children _____ outside.
e: Two simultaneous actions in the past. They are occurring at the same time. *Past progressive* for both.

q: If you are tired, you _____.
e: Advice. "Should" is a common modal when giving advice. If these questions are too easy, you *should go* to a higher level.

q: Before I came to DLI, I _____ English for 5 months.
e: Sometimes we can use *past progressive* to indicate a continuous action in the subsequent action in the simple past.

q: I _____ English before I came to DLI.
e: *Past perfect*. Two actions are in the past, one clearly *before* the other. The helping verb.

q: He _____ in Boston in 1982.
e: passive voice structure. His mother bore (carried) him inside her body. He was born (by his mother). Therefore, he *was born*.

q: While I was driving to work this morning, I _____ to the radio.
e: Two simultaneous actions in the past, both progressive (continuous).

q: Cpl. Whitfield _____ next week.
e: "Next week" requires *future tense*. *He will graduate*

q: You ought to go visit the Gateway Arch. You _____ go visit the Gateway Arch.
e: "Ought to" is a modal that means "*Should*." Advice recommendation.

q: By the time I graduate, I _____ at least 12 ECL tests.
e: *Future perfect*. I have not graduated yet. But by the time I do graduate, something else *will have* already *happened*.

q: He can sing well, _____?
e: *Tag* question. Affirmative "can" in the main clause takes negative "can't" in the tag. If you have a modal or helping verb, repeat that modal or helping verb in the tag.

q: This exercise _____ by Mr. Ashford.
e: *Passive voice*. The word "by" usually indicates a passive structure. Active voice: Mr. Ashford wrote this exercise.

q: By the time the firemen arrived, the flames _____ by the homeowner.
e: Two actions in the past. The first action (in time) can be *past perfect*. The subsequent action can be simple past.

q: While I was driving to work this morning, I _____ to my new Celine Dion Cassette.
e: Two actions happening simultaneously. Both can be in the *past progressive*.

q: If I _____ ECL-qualified, I would not have to do a lot of these extra exercises.
e: "*If*" clause. *Present unreal*. *If I were*

q: Before I could get back to the safety of my room, it _____.
e: The first action (rain) can be in the *past perfect*. *It had already begun* before something else happened.

q: Last week, he promised me that he _____ attend yesterday's meeting.
e: *Reported speech*. Main verb "promised" is in the past, so the subsequent verb "will" must shift to past "would.

q: The color red on the flag _____ blood.
e: Third person singular *the color* (*it*) symbolizes *present tense*

q: By the time you finally graduate from school, you _____ with 14 different teachers.
e: Future perfect tense One thing *will have happened* by the time something "ought we" in the tag. You must substitute the closest *modal* equivalent ("should").

q: Nary a drop of rain fell at the airport last night, _____?
e: "Nary" is a negative word. Put affirmative in the tag.

q: If Napoleon _____ more troops, he might not have lost at Waterloo.
e: *If* clause. Past unreal. If he had something

q: By this time tomorrow, I _____ at DLI for 72 hours.
e: Future perfect tense

q: The bill _____ to you before the end of the month.
e: Future tense, passive voice.

q: If I were the boss, I _____ you extra work.
e: Second conditional. If + past, would + base form.

q: I had the secretary _____ the letter five times before I was satisfied.
e: You have a person DO something, simple form of the verb.

q: We were just sitting down to dinner when the phone _____.
e: A past continuous action interrupted by a simple past tense verb. One thing was happening when something else happened.

q: My mother _____ down the stairs three times this summer.
e: Irregular verb. *Fall*. Present perfect tense.

q: If Craig really _____ at the meeting (and two people said they talked to him), I didn't see him there.
e: This is a *past real*. It is possible he was at the meeting. This is not an *unreal* situation.

q: _____ I to become a supervisor, I would probably not enjoy it.
e: A reduced "*If*" clause. If I were to become Were I to become

q: I saw the old man fatally _____ himself once through the heart.
e: You see and hear people "do" or "doing" something, but in this case we can't put the continuous act; it was instantaneous.

q: We liked the restaurant because we _____ quickly.
e: Past tense passive voice They served us quickly (active) = We were served quickly (passive).

q: My parents live _____ 253 Oak Street.
e: If you have the *number* and the street name, it takes *at*.

q: This exercise was written _____ Mr. Ashford.
e: Passive voice. The action is done *by* someone.

q: I would like to live _____ the country miles from the nearest town.
e: *In* the country In the city In a town

q: The students are waiting _____ the classroom.
e: A room takes *in*.

q: Americans celebrate Memorial Day _____ May.
e: A month by itself takes *in*.

q: I went there _____ 1996.
e: A year by itself takes *in*.

q: The Sears Tower is the tallest building _____ Chicago.
e: In the world In space In your imagination In the universe

q: In spite _____ the rain, we practiced for the parade.
e: prepositional phrase *in spite of*

q: He was born _____ 1982.
e: A year by itself takes *in*.

q: Thanksgiving is always celebrated _____ November.
e: A month by itself takes *in*.

q: He came to class _____ 0735 this morning.
e: Preposition of time. *At* a specific time.

q: The children are playing _____ the street again.
e: *In* the street It's a place with marked borders. An area with defined limits.

q: Capt. Barrow passed out dead drunk _____ the sidewalk near his car.
e: *On* the sidewalk. *In* the street.

q: Mr. Whitfield has been my teacher _____ Oct 24.
e: When you give the starting point for measuring time, we use *since*, especially with *present perfect verbs*.

q: My son drew pictures _____ the wall of his bedroom.
e: The pictures are touching the surface of the wall, so they are *on* the wall.

q: I have been here at DLI _____ 8 weeks.
e: When you have the total amount of time given, use *for* in these *present perfect* structures.

q: I have been here at DLI _____ October of last year.
e: Present perfect tense. When you have only the starting point for your measurement, use *since*.

q: Abraham Lincoln was assassinated _____ John Wilkes Booth in 1865.
e: passive voice! An action *is done by* someone.

q: Children should walk _____ the sidewalks.
e: *On* the sidewalk

q: Children should not walk _____ the streets.
e: *In* the street

q: My mother likes to take long walks _____ the evening.
e: Parts of the day take *in*.

q: He stayed _____ bed all day.
e: You are *in bed* when you have at least one of the covers *over* you (a sheet, a the surface with no covering over you.

q: I have been in the Army _____ 1993.
e: Present perfect. Only the starting point is given. *Use since*.

q: You should not walk alone in this neighborhood _____ night.
e: *In* the evening but *at* night

q: My father always takes a long nap _____ the afternoon.
e: part of the day *in* the morning *in* the afternoon *in* the evening

q: Don't sit with your elbows _____ the table.
e: touching the surface only *on* the table

q: He wants to go _____ school in Edinburgh.
e: You *go to* a school. *But*: You *attend* (no preposition) a college or university or school.

q: There is no one _____ the world who can help you now.
e: It's a place. *In* the world *ini* the universe *in* the solar system

q: There was a fire _____ the library yesterday.
e: inside a specific building *in* the dorms *in* the Riverside Inn

q: My wife is _____ work right now.
e: It's a place, so you can be *at* the place.

q: We might be able to travel quickly to the moon _____ the future.
e: a period of time *in* the past In the future

q: Cats like to sleep all day and prowl the neighborhoods _____ night.
e: in the morning in the afternoon in the evening *but* at night

q: All of these prepositions questions were written _____ Mr. Ashford.
e: passive voice

q: I was raised _____ the island of Nantucket.
e: *On* an island The island is *in* the water.

q: I have not seen a movie _____ five or six months.
e: When you give the total amount of time, you use *for*, especially in *present perfect* sentences.

q: I don't like to sit _____ Capt. Barrow.
e: *Sit by* someone. You can sit *beside* someone, but the word *besides* (with the "s" *Addition to*: Besides German and French, she can speak English.

q: Let's sit _____ the shade of that big tree over there.
e: *In* the shade *in* direct sunlight *in* a specific area

q: Don't stare _____ strangers. It's not polite.
e: Preposition of direction. You *stare at point at look at a* rhinoceros can *charge at* you.

q: Sign your name _____ block 21 at the bottom of this page.
e: The block has a perimeter, so you put your signature *in* the block.

q: Turn right _____ the next intersection.
e: place *turn at* the sign *turn at* the traffic light.

q: There was a body lying _____ the middle of the road.
e: area *in* the middle of the room *in* the middle of the hall

q: I will do it _____ pleasure.
e: preposition of manner You do something *with* a certain attitude *with gusto with reluctance with enthusiasm*

q: Neil Armstrong was the first earthling to walk _____ the moon.
e: touching the surface *on* the moon *on* the floor On the ground

q: He makes a living _____ recycling old newspaper and magazines.
e: preposition of manner. *How* did he do something? You can do something *by* doing for 4 days. He excelled by writing a brilliant essay.

q: He has served _____ the government for twenty years.
e: You serve *in* an organization.

q: The contractors are going to tear _____ the old road and replace it with a modern 4-lane one.
e: The road is lying flat *on* the ground, so you have to tear it *up*.

q: They will not qualify him because his ECL is still _____ 80.
e: A number can be *below* or *under* another number. He can't buy alcohol; he's still *under* 21. I wish I could keep my weight *below* 165.

q: I went to Cleveland _____ the weekend.
e: for a period of time or two days or 48 hours

q: He is serving as a cabinet member _____ present.
e: at present or at the present time

q: Who is serving _____ the CO of that unit now?
e: *As* means "in the capacity of."

q: Capt. Whitfield wants to play _____ the basketball team.
e: We play *on* a name, because our names can be written *on* the team roster, *on* the paper that lists our names.

q: I did it _____ the spur of the moment.
e: You do something *on impulse on* the spur of the moment

q: I heard some bad news _____ the radio this morning.
e: *On* the radio There was a good show *on* Channel 4 last night. I found a good story *on* the Internet.

q: We can have the meeting in Room 204 if the door _____.
e: passive voice structure

q: If I _____ in your position, I would not do that.
e: present unreal subjunctive *if I were*

q: If I were a person who _____ a million dollars, I would retire immediately.
e: This is tricky. You are a person. The unreal part of it is having a million dollars. *If I were a person who had* .

q: We were delayed because of all *the red tape*.
e: *Red tape* is governmental bureaucratic delays that slow you down. Apparently in the paper, much less process it.

q: How does it feel to be *low man on the totem pole*?
o: the person with the least seniority
the richest person in the group
the smartest person in the organization
e: often the newest person in the organization. This comes from native American Indian culture.

q: Craig looks *down in the dumps* today.
e: *Down in the dumps* = unhappy = sad = dejected = in a depressing situation, as if one is *living in the dump*.

q: Relax! *Go with the flow*.
e: *Go with the flow* = do what everyone else is doing and don't argue about it = do what everyone wants you t

q: Craig answers the questions correctly *once in a blue moon*.
e: A blue moon is very rare. Once in a blue moon is very rare. How often have you looked up in the sky and seen a *blue* moon up there?

q: Don't assign that duty to Craig. He's still *wet behind the ears*.
e: *Wet behind the ears* = inexperienced, too new at the job. Like a new-born baby who was dried with a towel, but nobody dried behind the ears.

q: The next ECL will _____ easy.
e: simple form of a verb after a *modal will be might be should be*

q: Yesterday, I _____ tardy for class because my car wouldn't start.
e: yesterday = past tense Yesterday *I was*

q: I was born _____ August.
e: A month by itself takes *in*.

q: The teacher _____ all day yesterday preparing new handouts for you.
e: yesterday = past tense third person singular *the teacher worked*

q: The next book quiz will be _____ Wednesday.
e: Day by itself takes *on*.

q: What will you _____ tomorrow night?
e: modal Put simple form after a modal. You will *do* what?

q: Don't let the children play _____ the street.
e: *In* the street *on* the sidewalk

q: These drugs must be given top the patients under _____ conditions.
e: passive voice structure The conditions are controlled by someone, so they are *controlled* conditions.

q: I _____ finishing the report right now.
e: right now = present progressive *I AM finishing*.

q: We had an _____ lesson yesterday. It was about biology.
e: word form = interesting The lesson was interesting. The students were interested in the lesson.

q: I believe the waitress dropped _____ pencil on the floor.
e: Since a waitress is a woman and the pencil belongs to her, it is *her pencil*.

q: It _____ twenty minutes to drive from here to the airport.
e: third person singular present tense *it takes*

q: Last night, I _____ for nine hours.
e: Last night = past tense. Irregular verb *sleep slept* Last night, *I slept*

q: When you are finished with your conversation, _____ the phone.
e: instructions or orders in the imperative (You) hang up the phone.

q: My favorite season of the year is *autumn*.
e: seasons of the year *fall* = *autumn* (September, October, November in the U.S.)

q: I need to go to the dentist because _____
o: I have a pain in my ankle.
e: dentist = person who works on the *teeth*.

q: America _____ by Columbus in 1492.
e: passive voice

q: Do you know _____?
o: who is owner of this book
e: After certain connecting words in complex sentences the correct word order is *subject*/*verb*. Can you tell me where *the hotel is*?

q: I haven't seen my family _____ October 23.
e: When you give only the starting point of measuring the time, use "since" in these October 25.

q: Please give this package to _____.
e: "*To*" is a preposition. You need *object* forms because this is *object* of a Craig. Give the package to *joe* and *her*.

q: The escaped prisoner _____ last night near the airport.
e: past tense (*last night*) passive voice

q: I haven't visited the Gateway Arch _____.
e: In a negative *present perfect* or *past perfect* construction, put "yet" at the end. I haven't passed the ECL yet.

q: I _____ sick right now.
e: irregular verb = resent tense. *I feel* happy. *I feel* sick.

q: I stayed up all night, _____ I feel very tired today.
e: One clause is the result of the other. There is a comma between the clauses, so you use "*Therefore*." It was extremely hot, so we went swimming.

q: Please give the message to _____.
e: object forms required objects of preposition Give the message to *him*. Give the message to *his wife*.

q: All of these sentences _____ by Mr. Ashford.
e: passive voice The subject is plural. The sentences *were written* by someone.

q: _____ military students must wear uniforms to class.
e: *Stundents* is a count noun in the *plural*. The only determiner that fits is *all*.

q: Blake is 17 years old. Neil is 18 years old. Craig is 16 years old.
e: Based on the facts given, the comparison between Craig and Neil is the only one that is younger than Neil (18).

q: This question _____ for you by Mr. Ashford.
e: *Passive voice* . Something *is done* by somebody. *Past tense* of the *passive*. It *was done* by somebody.

q: This book _____ by William Faulkner in 1953.
e: passive voice. Requires the "be" auxiliary. Past tense.

q: I have been here _____ two months.
e: starting point, you use "*Since*." I have been here *since* April 5.

q: Yesterday, the news about the earthquakes in Chile and Peru _____bad.
e: yesterday = past tense . *The news* = singular *the news was bad*.

q: Why is Craig looking under the hood? Because _____.
e: hood = the part of the car that you lift up to look at the engine.

q: If I finish my homework early, I _____ to the gym and work out.
e: *If* clause *future* might = possibility (*will* = future certainty)

q: I was unable to go to the movie with my friends last night.
e: Last Night = past tense. Only answer B is in the past. If I was unable to go, then I didn't go.

q: I have been *at DLI* _____ six months.
e: combined amount of time. Use "for" in these kinds of present perfect sentences.

q: If I _____ you, I would be more careful with my answers.
e: *Subjunctive* "*If*" clause present unreal. If *I were* you, I would study the "*If*" clause patterns.

q: Craig said that we have to be at Lab 3 before 0800, _____?
e: tag question Craig said: didn't he? Affirmative in the main clause needs negative in the tag.

q: I am here _____ your teacher, not _____ your parent.
e: *As* = preposition of capacity (in the capacity of) He will be acting *as* the company commander for three weeks.

q: I hear a lot of police sirens. Someone _____ have committed a crime nearby.
e: *Inference modal* Based on some evidence, you come to a logical conclusion.

q: Shouldn't those rose bushes _____ more water?
e: The modal *should* is here, and you must put simple form of a verb after a modal.

q: My cousin Dominic _____ 21 years in the Marine Corps before retiring.
e: past tense. He *spent* years in the Corps before he retired.

q: It is not polite to stare _____ strangers.
e: preposition of direction. You stare *at* You look *at* You point *at*

q: My room is _____ the third floor of the dorm.
e: Something is *on* the floor, touching the surface of the floor.

q: That car Capt. Barrow just bought cost a lot, _____?
e: The car cost a lot (past tenses), *didn't it*?

q: I don't like the new printers _____ they're not as fast as the old ones.
e: since = because The second clause tells us *why*, so we need *because* or *since*.

q: If I had known the answers, I _____ well on the test.
e: *Past unreal conditional*.

q: The package _____ today. Otherwise, it won't get there for my mother's birthday.
e: Passive voice is requited here. *Must be mailed*.

q: I just heard some bad news _____ the radio.
e: *On* the radio *on* the television

q: The battle for Nevada independence took place _____.
e: This is an action in the past expressed in the simple past, so it happened "years ago.

q: That car is relatively inexpensive. _____, I think you should buy it.
e: *Cause* and *effect*. The car is not expensive, *so* you should buy it. "Therefore" is punctuation. You are studying a lot. *Therefore*, you should do well on the next test.

q: All of the cake _____ by the dog in no time at all.
e: passive voice. The verb must agree with "cake."

q: All of the cakes _____ by the officers' wives.
e: passive voice. The verb must agree with "cakes."

q: If Craig _____ here, he could help us.
e: Conditional present unreal *if joe were* There is an entire section of "*If'* clauses in this databank *if you want to try them*.

q: Several soldiers _____ being reassigned to this unit next week.
e: plural subject , future (next week) *progressive passive they are being reassigned*

q: If I _____ ECL-qualified, I would not have to do these exercises.
e: *If* clause *unreal* present If *I were*

q: The policeman ordered that Craig _____ out of the car with his hands up.
e: After certain *verbs* of *urgency*, a "that" clause takes a subjunctive (simple) form.

q: Craig bought _____ for his fiancée.
e: *A dozen things*, not a dozen *of* things. However, you can say *a couple of a dozen of roses*.

q: I visited my family _____ Christmas.
e: preposition of time *for* a short period of *time*.

q: When I was a child, *I used to* eat candy all day long.
e: used to = would To have done something in the past but not now.

q: The Commander ordered that Capt. Barrow _____ in the company area at 0500 tomorrow morning.
e: After certain *verbs* of *urgency*, you have to put *simple form* in the "that" clause. The policeman *insisted* that Craig *get* out of the car with his hands up.

q: I would like to have a neighbor _____ I can feel certain will watch my apartment when I'm away.
e: The word in the blank must be a *subject* form *he* or *she will watch* my apartment. *Whom* will not fit here.

q: It is mandatory that Capt. Barrow _____ at the airport before 0600 tomorrow.
e: It is imperative that he *get* 80 on the next ECL.

q: Blake can't find his key. It _____ out of his pocket.
e: *May* = modal of possibility You are suggesting that this is one of the things that *may*, *might*, or *could* have happened.

q: My mother asked, Whose shoes are those? My mother wants to know _____.
e: Reported speech. After the connecting words "whose shoes," the subject "those" must

q: _____, I would have helped you.
e: This is the *reduced subjuntive*. "If I had been there" can be reduced to "Had I been there.

q: You _____ bring your own pencils to the testing room. We will provide the pencils.
e: This is a modal. "He need not" do something = He doesn't need to do it. You need not do it = You don't need to do it.

q: By the time you graduate, you _____ at least 40 tests.
e: future perfect tense By the time I retire, I will have worked for this company for 35 years.

q: Before _____, he meditated for three minutes.
e: "*Before*" is a preposition of time here. You need a noun after it. "Starting" is the gerund or noun form of "to start.

q: _____ any documents you need me to sign before the meeting starts?
e: Use *there is / there are* to say that something exists. *Documents* is plural, so *are there*.

q: _____ a spare uniform in the storeroom, or should I order one?
e: *Is there* introduces the existence of a single object. *Is it* would refer to something already identified.

q: _____ enough fuel in the tank to reach the base?
e: *Fuel* is uncountable, so the singular form *is there* is required.

q: Nadia has worked at the hospital ever _____ she graduated.
e: *Ever since* links a present situation to its starting point in the past.

q: The two units have trained together ever _____ the exercise in Bizerte.
e: *Since* introduces the point when the situation began. *Ago* follows a length of time.

q: He has not touched a cigarette ever _____ the doctor warned him.
e: *Since* introduces the starting point of an unfinished period.

q: Let's _____ certain the radios are working before we move out.
e: After *let's*, the verb takes its base form, with no *to*.

q: Let's _____ the briefing at eight so that everyone can attend.
e: *Let's* is followed by the bare infinitive.

q: Let's not _____ the decision until we have the full report.
e: The negative form is *let's not* + base form.

q: The major expects _____ the report before Friday.
e: *Expect* takes an object followed by the full infinitive: expect somebody to do something.

q: Nobody expected _____ so quickly.
e: The pattern is *expect + object + to + base form*.

q: The instructor expects _____ on time every morning.
e: *Expect* requires an object before the infinitive.

q: Of all the candidates, Adrian performed _____.
e: *Of all* calls for the superlative. *Better* compares only two.

q: Samira speaks _____ of the three interpreters.
e: With three or more, use the superlative *the most clearly*.

q: This is _____ route to the airport at this hour.
e: Short adjectives form the superlative with *-est*: the fastest.

q: They never finished the inventory, _____?
e: *Never* makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive and in the past: did they.

q: She hardly spoke during the meeting, _____?
e: *Hardly* carries a negative meaning, so the tag is positive.

q: You have never visited Sousse, _____?
e: The statement is in the present perfect and negative, so the tag is *have you*.

q: The runway _____ when the delegation landed.
e: An action in progress in the past, interrupted by another, takes the past continuous, here in the passive.

q: The files _____ when the power failed.
e: Past continuous passive: *was/were being* + past participle.

q: Dinner _____ when the first guests arrived.
e: The action was under way at that past moment, so the past continuous passive is used.

q: _____ for twelve hours, she still insisted on finishing the inspection.
e: *Even though* introduces a full clause with a subject and a verb. *Despite* cannot.

q: _____ the heavy rain, the parade went ahead as planned.
e: *Despite* is followed by a noun. *Although* would require a clause.

q: _____ he had trained for months, he failed the swimming test.
e: Only *even though* can introduce a subject and a conjugated verb.

q: We set out before dawn _____ the checkpoint queues.
e: Purpose is expressed by *in order to* + base form.

q: She stayed late _____ the presentation.
e: *In order to* + base form states the aim of the action.

q: They moved the antenna _____ a stronger signal.
e: The correct pattern for purpose is *in order to* + base form.

q: The commander insisted that every officer _____ the new procedure.
e: After *insist that*, the verb stays in its base form for every person. This is the subjunctive.

q: The doctor recommended that he _____ more rest.
e: *Recommend that* is followed by the base form, with no -s in the third person.

q: The committee demanded that the report _____ immediately.
e: The subjunctive passive is *be* + past participle: that it be published.

q: The ceremony begins at nine and the colonel _____ the medals shortly afterwards.
e: The future continuous describes an action in progress at a stated future moment.

q: Do not call at seven; we _____ dinner then.
e: *Will be* + -ing places the action in progress at that future time.

q: This time next week I _____ across the Atlantic.
e: *This time next week* points to a future moment, so the future continuous is used.

q: The secret _____ a good soufflé is patience.
e: *The secret to* and *the key to* are followed by a noun or an -ing form.

q: There is no objection _____ the meeting to Tuesday.
e: *Objection to* is followed by an -ing form.

q: He is not accustomed _____ so early.
e: *Accustomed to* is a preposition, so the verb takes the -ing form.

q: She chose _____ by train rather than by plane.
e: *Choose* is followed by the full infinitive.

q: They decided _____ the launch until spring.
e: *Decide* takes the full infinitive.

q: He refused _____ the document without a lawyer.
e: *Refuse* is followed by *to* + base form.

q: By the time you land in Tunis, we _____ the preparations.
e: *By the time* sets a deadline, so the future perfect is required.

q: By next summer, Lucas _____ here for ten years.
e: The future perfect expresses a duration completed by a future point.

q: By Friday, the crew _____ all the equipment.
e: *By Friday* marks a deadline: future perfect.

q: They _____ the whole report already! It was only assigned this morning.
e: *Can't have* + past participle expresses certainty that something did not happen.

q: She _____ the message; her phone was switched off all day.
e: Deduction that a past event was impossible: *can't have* + past participle.

q: He _____ the keys here; I checked the desk twice.
e: *Can't have left* states that it was impossible for him to have done so.

q: Amine, it is high time you _____ for the examination.
e: *It is time you* is followed by the past simple, although it refers to the present.

q: It is time we _____ this discussion.
e: The pattern *it is time* + subject + past simple expresses that something is overdue.

q: It is about time the roof _____ repaired.
e: *It is about time* takes the past simple, here with the passive: was repaired.

q: The whole wing _____ because the inspectors arrive tomorrow.
e: Present perfect passive: *has been* + past participle. The result matters now.

q: The proposal _____ by the board.
e: The subject undergoes the action, so the passive is required.

q: All the vehicles _____ this week.
e: Plural subject in the present perfect passive: *have been* + past participle.

q: You _____ us! We waited two hours at the station.
e: *Could have* + past participle criticises something that was possible but not done.

q: She _____ the truth; nobody would have blamed her.
e: The opportunity existed in the past and was missed: *could have told*.

q: They _____ the meeting here; the room was free all morning.
e: *Could have held* refers to an unrealised possibility in the past.

q: I do not remember _____ that decision. When was it taken?
e: *Remember* + -ing refers to a memory of something already done. With the infinitive it would mean not forgetting to do it.

q: Do you remember _____ him at the conference in Zurich?
e: *Remember meeting* recalls a past event.

q: She remembered _____ the door, but the alarm went off anyway.
e: The -ing form shows she recalls the action she performed.

q: I wish I _____ the contract without reading it.
e: *Wish* + past perfect expresses regret about a past action.

q: She wishes she _____ the earlier flight.
e: Regret about a past choice: *wish* + past perfect.

q: They wish they _____ so much at the auction.
e: *Wish* + past perfect looks back on something they now regret.

q: The officer _____ you were speaking to is our new liaison.
e: *Whom* is used when the relative pronoun is the object of a preposition.

q: The colleague with _____ I share an office has just retired.
e: After a preposition, only *whom* is possible for a person.

q: The candidate _____ we interviewed yesterday accepted the post.
e: *Whom* is the object of *interviewed*. *Which* refers to things.

q: If only Nadia _____ how to swim before the trip.
e: *If only* + past perfect expresses regret about the past.

q: If only we _____ the warning seriously.
e: Regret about something not done in the past: *if only* + past perfect.

q: If only he _____ earlier, he would have caught the train.
e: This is a third conditional: *had left* in the if-clause, *would have caught* in the main clause.
